chapter: Detroit 1927: Pollack, Casa Loma, Atlantic City
title: Atlantic City: still no direction from management
summary: At Atlantic City he did few arrangements because no one directed the band's writing.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So anyway, we got down to Atlantic City in August, the Goldkette band, and I did very few arrange-

ments down there, because I think I started to say before the Goldkette band wasn't very well organized and -- from the administrative standpoint. There was no one there that was -- to say 'We are going in this direction, I want to make six arrangements and we'll go out and try to record them,' anything like that. We're going to lay on a job like in Atlantic City, and there was no incentive, nothing to say, 'Bill, do this or do that, or do whatever you want,' or something like that.

You would have to go around, hang around and wait to find out through different ways what should be done here. But yet they wanted you around. They wanted you to be around for any kind of recording that had to be done, and that used to irk me a little bit, because you feel as if you're not doing anything, not contributing.
